metadata.scope: Specialist companies, experts, and subdomains in non-AI analytics. This is a reviewed seed, not an exhaustive claim.
exclusions: general cloud and diversified technology vendors
LLM, generative-AI, conversational-BI, RAG, and agentic-analytics capabilities
metadata.entity_model: Domains contain analytics types. Companies and experts link many-to-many to analytics types. Direct expert-company relationships are separate evidence-bearing records.

domains.name: Process and case analytics
domains.definition: Analysis of event data to discover, check, compare, simulate, and improve operational processes and individual process cases.

domains.name: Causal inference and experimentation
domains.definition: Methods that estimate the effect of interventions, policies, product changes, or treatments rather than correlation alone.

domains.name: Customer and product analytics
domains.definition: Measurement of customer value, behavior, retention, journeys, product usage, and digital experience.

domains.name: Marketing and commercial measurement
domains.definition: Measurement of marketing, advertising, price, promotion, assortment, and revenue-growth effects.

domains.name: Decision and optimization analytics
domains.definition: Mathematical optimization, simulation, and operations-research methods used to recommend or select actions.

domains.name: Privacy-preserving analytics
domains.definition: Analytics architectures and mathematical controls designed to limit disclosure, tracking, or transfer of sensitive data.

domains.name: Semantic, metrics, and embedded analytics
domains.definition: Governed definitions and delivery layers that make consistent analytics reusable across tools and applications.

domains.name: Analytics engineering and data trust
domains.definition: Engineering, testing, lineage, contracts, and reliability practices that make analytical outputs reproducible and trustworthy.

domains.name: Operational and real-time analytics
domains.definition: Low-latency measurement and activation that moves analytical results into operational systems and workflows.

domains.name: Local, browser, visual, and data-app analytics
domains.definition: Interactive analytical computation and communication performed locally, in browsers, notebooks, or purpose-built data applications.

domains.name: Risk, fraud, and financial analytics
domains.definition: Quantitative measurement of credit, fraud, insurance, market, liquidity, and financial performance risks.
known_gaps: expert list not yet deeply reviewed

domains.name: Supply-chain and retail analytics
domains.definition: Demand, inventory, logistics, pricing, promotion, assortment, and retail customer measurement.

domains.name: Geospatial, climate, and sustainability analytics
domains.definition: Location, spatial, environmental, physical climate-risk, emissions, and sustainability measurement.

domains.name: Healthcare and life-sciences analytics
domains.definition: Clinical, observational, trial, patient, health-market, and pharmaceutical commercial analytics.

domains.name: People and organizational analytics
domains.definition: Measurement of workforce composition, retention, performance, collaboration, skills, and organizational networks.

analytics_types.name: Process discovery
analytics_types.definition: Constructing process models from observed event sequences.

analytics_types.name: Conformance checking
analytics_types.definition: Comparing observed behavior with a reference process or rule set.

analytics_types.name: Case-level inspection
analytics_types.definition: Inspecting the events, attributes, timing, and path of an individual process instance.

analytics_types.name: Object-centric process mining
analytics_types.definition: Analyzing events linked to multiple interacting business objects rather than one flattened case identifier.

analytics_types.name: Task mining
analytics_types.definition: Analyzing user-level task events across desktop and application interactions.

analytics_types.name: Process simulation
analytics_types.definition: Simulating process designs, resources, queues, and timing to evaluate proposed changes.

analytics_types.name: Process performance analytics
analytics_types.definition: Measuring bottlenecks, cycle time, waiting time, rework, and resource utilization.

analytics_types.name: Causal inference
analytics_types.definition: Estimating intervention effects from experimental or observational data under explicit assumptions.

analytics_types.name: Online controlled experiments
analytics_types.definition: Randomized digital experiments that compare product or experience variants.

analytics_types.name: Quasi-experimental analytics
analytics_types.definition: Causal designs using natural experiments, discontinuities, panels, or comparison groups without direct randomization.

analytics_types.name: Geographic experimentation
analytics_types.definition: Estimating incremental effects using treated and control geographic markets.

analytics_types.name: Customer-base and lifetime-value analytics
analytics_types.definition: Probabilistic measurement of customer acquisition, retention, transactions, and future economic value.

analytics_types.name: Product behavioral analytics
analytics_types.definition: Event-based analysis of how users and accounts interact with a digital product.

analytics_types.name: Funnel and cohort analytics
analytics_types.definition: Comparing conversion paths, retention, and behavior across user cohorts.

analytics_types.name: Session replay analytics
analytics_types.definition: Reconstructing digital sessions to inspect experience, friction, and errors.

analytics_types.name: Customer-journey analytics
analytics_types.definition: Analyzing sequences of customer interactions across channels and lifecycle stages.

analytics_types.name: Marketing-mix modeling
analytics_types.definition: Estimating aggregate contributions and response curves for marketing investments and external factors.

analytics_types.name: Marketing incrementality analytics
analytics_types.definition: Estimating outcomes caused by marketing that would not otherwise have occurred.

analytics_types.name: Marketing attribution
analytics_types.definition: Assigning conversion or revenue credit across marketing contacts and channels.

analytics_types.name: Pricing and promotion analytics
analytics_types.definition: Measuring price elasticity, promotional response, cannibalization, and optimal commercial actions.

analytics_types.name: Revenue-growth-management analytics
analytics_types.definition: Integrated pricing, promotion, assortment, pack, and trade-investment analytics.

analytics_types.name: Mathematical optimization
analytics_types.definition: Selecting decisions subject to objectives, constraints, and mathematical models.

analytics_types.name: Robust and stochastic optimization
analytics_types.definition: Optimization under uncertainty, distributions, or bounded parameter variation.

analytics_types.name: Scheduling and routing analytics
analytics_types.definition: Optimizing sequences, assignments, routes, capacities, and resource use.

analytics_types.name: Decision simulation
analytics_types.definition: Evaluating policies and scenarios through mathematical or discrete-event simulation.

analytics_types.name: Differentially private analytics
analytics_types.definition: Statistical analysis with a formal bound on information revealed about any individual record.

analytics_types.name: Data clean-room analytics
analytics_types.definition: Controlled collaboration and aggregate analysis across parties without unrestricted raw-data access.

analytics_types.name: Cookieless aggregate web analytics
analytics_types.definition: Web measurement without persistent visitor identifiers or cross-site profiles.

analytics_types.name: Self-hosted analytics
analytics_types.definition: Analytics deployed on infrastructure controlled by the data owner.

analytics_types.name: Universal semantic layer
analytics_types.definition: A reusable layer of governed entities, dimensions, joins, access rules, and business definitions.

analytics_types.name: Metrics store
analytics_types.definition: A centralized, queryable system for governed metric definitions and calculations.

analytics_types.name: Headless BI
analytics_types.definition: Analytics logic and query services exposed independently of a fixed visualization interface.

analytics_types.name: Embedded analytics
analytics_types.definition: Governed analytics incorporated into another software product or workflow.

analytics_types.name: Analytics engineering
analytics_types.definition: Applying modular code, version control, testing, documentation, and deployment practices to analytics transformations.

analytics_types.name: Data testing
analytics_types.definition: Executable assertions about schema, values, relationships, freshness, and business rules.

analytics_types.name: Data lineage and impact analysis
analytics_types.definition: Tracking how datasets and analytical outputs are produced and what depends on them.

analytics_types.name: Data contracts
analytics_types.definition: Explicit agreements covering data structure, semantics, quality, service levels, and use.

analytics_types.name: Data observability
analytics_types.definition: Monitoring freshness, volume, schema, lineage, quality, and downstream data reliability.

analytics_types.name: Reverse ETL
analytics_types.definition: Synchronizing governed warehouse data into operational applications.

analytics_types.name: Streaming data activation
analytics_types.definition: Low-latency synchronization and triggering from changing analytical data.

analytics_types.name: Composable customer-data analytics
analytics_types.definition: Using the warehouse as the customer source of truth with modular identity, audience, and activation services.

analytics_types.name: Real-time operational analytics
analytics_types.definition: Continuously updated measures, alerts, and applications used during operations.

analytics_types.name: In-process analytical processing
analytics_types.definition: Columnar analytical SQL embedded inside an application process rather than accessed through a separate database server.

analytics_types.name: In-browser analytical SQL
analytics_types.definition: Analytical query execution inside a web browser, commonly through WebAssembly.

analytics_types.name: Interactive data applications
analytics_types.definition: Purpose-built interactive analytical interfaces combining computation, visualization, narrative, and controls.

analytics_types.name: Data visualization
analytics_types.definition: Visual encoding and interaction designed to support data exploration, explanation, and communication.

analytics_types.name: Credit-risk analytics
analytics_types.definition: Measuring borrower default, exposure, loss, and portfolio credit risk.

analytics_types.name: Fraud analytics
analytics_types.definition: Detecting and measuring suspicious transactions, claims, identities, or behaviors.

analytics_types.name: Actuarial and insurance analytics
analytics_types.definition: Quantifying insurance risk, pricing, reserves, claims, and capital requirements.

analytics_types.name: Supply-chain analytics
analytics_types.definition: Measuring and optimizing supply, demand, inventory, procurement, logistics, and service levels.

analytics_types.name: Retail and assortment analytics
analytics_types.definition: Analyzing customers, products, stores, categories, baskets, assortment, and merchandising.

analytics_types.name: Geospatial analytics
analytics_types.definition: Analyzing spatial relationships, movement, location, proximity, and geographic patterns.

analytics_types.name: Physical climate-risk analytics
analytics_types.definition: Quantifying asset-level exposure and vulnerability to climate hazards under scenarios.

analytics_types.name: Sustainability and emissions analytics
analytics_types.definition: Measuring environmental performance, greenhouse-gas inventories, targets, and disclosures.

analytics_types.name: Clinical-trial analytics
analytics_types.definition: Design, operational measurement, monitoring, and statistical analysis of clinical trials.

analytics_types.name: Real-world evidence analytics
analytics_types.definition: Analysis of observational health data to evaluate utilization, safety, and comparative effectiveness.

analytics_types.name: Pharmaceutical commercial analytics
analytics_types.definition: Market, territory, patient, prescriber, launch, and sales analytics for life sciences.

analytics_types.name: Healthcare market analytics
analytics_types.definition: Measurement of providers, organizations, utilization, referral patterns, and market structure.

analytics_types.name: People analytics
analytics_types.definition: Quantitative analysis of workforce composition, hiring, performance, engagement, and retention.

analytics_types.name: Organizational-network analytics
analytics_types.definition: Analysis of collaboration and communication relationships within and across organizations.

innovations.name: Object-centric process mining
innovations.description: Replaces the single-case view of classical process mining with events connected to multiple interacting objects, preserving many-to-many operational relationships.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Event models, graph and relational structures, formal process models, and deterministic discovery or conformance algorithms.

innovations.name: OCEL 2.0 object-centric event-log standard
innovations.description: Adds changing object attributes, explicit object-to-object relationships, qualified relationships, and interoperable relational, XML, and JSON representations.
innovations.non_ai_basis: A formal event-data metamodel and exchange formats; no learned model is required.

innovations.name: Integrated process-intelligence suites
innovations.description: Combines discovery, conformance, case inspection, performance analysis, task mining, and simulation in one evidence chain rather than isolated tools.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Event-log reconstruction, reference-model comparison, descriptive performance metrics, and discrete-event simulation.

innovations.name: Warehouse-native product analytics
innovations.description: Runs behavioral analysis directly on governed warehouse tables instead of requiring a second proprietary event store and duplicate ingestion pipeline.
innovations.non_ai_basis: SQL pushdown, warehouse data models, identity joins, and conventional behavioral aggregations.

innovations.name: Warehouse-native experimentation
innovations.description: Calculates experiment exposures, metrics, variance reduction, and statistical results over data that remains in the customer's warehouse.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Randomization, SQL aggregation, hypothesis testing, CUPED, confidence intervals, and sequential-testing statistics.

innovations.name: Universal metrics and semantic layers
innovations.description: Moves governed metrics and business semantics outside an individual dashboard so definitions can be reused across analytical consumers.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Declarative metric definitions, entity relationships, dimensional models, query planning, and access-control rules.

innovations.name: Headless and API-first BI
innovations.description: Separates analytical models, query execution, caching, and governance from the presentation layer and exposes them through APIs.
innovations.non_ai_basis: SQL, REST and GraphQL interfaces, caching, pre-aggregation, and declarative semantic models.

innovations.name: Semantic models and metrics as code
innovations.description: Stores metric definitions, joins, entities, and access rules in version-controlled files that can be reviewed, tested, and deployed.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Software version control, declarative configuration, compilation, tests, and continuous integration.

innovations.name: Software-engineering workflow for analytics
innovations.description: Makes modular transformations, dependency graphs, tests, documentation, pull requests, and CI/CD normal parts of analytical production.
innovations.non_ai_basis: SQL transformations and conventional software-engineering controls.

innovations.name: OpenLineage event standard
innovations.description: Introduces a vendor-neutral event model and API for recording datasets, jobs, runs, and their production relationships across tools.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Structured metadata events, identifiers, schemas, and deterministic dependency relationships.

innovations.name: Open data-contract specifications
innovations.description: Formalizes producer-consumer agreements for schema, semantics, quality, freshness, service levels, and permitted use in machine-readable documents.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Schemas, policy assertions, service-level metadata, and deterministic validation.

innovations.name: Warehouse-to-application reverse ETL
innovations.description: Turns modeled warehouse tables into operational records in CRM, marketing, support, advertising, and business applications.
innovations.non_ai_basis: SQL selection, field mapping, incremental synchronization, API delivery, and state reconciliation.

innovations.name: Streaming reverse ETL
innovations.description: Reduces activation latency by responding to warehouse changes and synchronizing them to operational destinations without waiting for full scheduled batches.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Change-data capture, streaming tables, incremental state comparison, and destination APIs.

innovations.name: Warehouse-centered composable CDP
innovations.description: Uses the existing warehouse as the customer record and assembles modular identity, audience, governance, and activation components around it.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Identity rules, SQL models, deterministic audience definitions, connectors, and APIs.

innovations.name: Analytical SQL inside the browser
innovations.description: Brings a columnar analytical database, Parquet and Arrow support, and query-driven partial file reads into browser processes through WebAssembly.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Vectorized query execution, WebAssembly, columnar formats, SQL, and browser workers.

innovations.name: Collaborative notebook-to-data-app workflow
innovations.description: Connects exploratory SQL or Python notebooks, multiplayer editing, versioning, interactive controls, and stakeholder-facing analytical applications.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Notebooks, SQL and Python runtimes, visualization grammars, permissions, and application layouts.

innovations.name: Code-first precomputed data applications
innovations.description: Builds interactive reports and dashboards as deployable static applications with data loaders that precompute snapshots for fast delivery.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Build systems, data loaders, Markdown, JavaScript, SQL, conventional visualization, and static hosting.

innovations.name: Commercial data clean rooms
innovations.description: Enables multiple parties to perform approved joins, aggregates, measurement, and activation without unrestricted exchange of row-level data.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Access controls, cryptography, isolated computation, query policies, aggregation thresholds, and auditing.

innovations.name: Interoperable private join and activation
innovations.description: Defines common guidance and protocols for private audience joins and activation across clean-room implementations.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Standard identifiers, cryptographic or controlled joins, policy enforcement, and interoperable request formats.

innovations.name: Cookieless aggregate web analytics
innovations.description: Measures site traffic and events without persistent identifiers, cross-site tracking, or user profiles, often with self-hosting options.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Aggregate counters, short-lived or daily uniqueness calculations, event collection, and conventional reporting.

innovations.name: Unified feature flags and controlled experimentation
innovations.description: Connects deterministic feature exposure, staged rollout, random assignment, metric calculation, and experiment decision records in one product workflow.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Hash-based assignment, randomization, hypothesis tests, sequential analysis, and governed metrics.

innovations.name: Governed embedded analytics services
innovations.description: Delivers tenant-aware metrics, dashboards, and exploration inside third-party products while retaining centralized semantics and permissions.
innovations.non_ai_basis: Semantic models, row-level security, tenant isolation, embedding APIs, and query caching.
